common_name: Snow Bunting Crocus (White with Lilac Feathering)

planting.note: Plant corms in fall in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Snow Bunting is an early-blooming species crocus, flowering ahead of the larger Dutch hybrids and naturalizing readily in lawns and rock gardens.

directions: Plant corms in fall in well-drained, average soil in full sun; good drainage prevents corm rot during summer dormancy. Snow Bunting produces small, fragrant, creamy-white flowers delicately feathered with soft lilac-purple on the outer petals and a bright orange-yellow throat, opening among the earliest crocus of the year, often before the last snow has fully melted in colder climates. Its small scale and early bloom make it well suited to naturalizing in a lawn, rock garden, or the front of a border where it can be enjoyed up close before larger spring bulbs take over the show. Allow the grass-like foliage to die back naturally after bloom before mowing over a naturalized planting, and it will multiply steadily by cormlets to form larger drifts over the years.

common_name: Cream Beauty Crocus (Creamy Yellow Species Crocus)

planting.note: Plant corms in fall in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Cream Beauty is an early, fragrant species crocus that naturalizes readily in lawns and rock gardens.

directions: Plant corms in fall in well-drained, average soil in full sun; good drainage is essential to prevent corm rot during summer dormancy. Cream Beauty bears soft, buttery cream-yellow flowers with a deeper gold-orange throat and a light honey fragrance, opening early in spring among the first bulbs to bloom and closing on cold or cloudy days to protect the pollen and reproductive parts inside. Its gentle color pairs beautifully with the deeper purples and blues of other early species crocus for a mixed naturalized planting. Allow the narrow, grass-like foliage to die back completely after flowering before mowing over lawn plantings, and it will slowly multiply by cormlets to form larger, denser drifts over the years without needing to be dug and divided.

common_name: Blue Pearl Crocus (Pale Silvery-Blue Species Crocus)

planting.note: Plant corms in fall in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Blue Pearl is an early species crocus with a distinctive bronze-yellow base color on the outer petals.

directions: Plant corms in fall in well-drained, average soil in full sun; good drainage prevents corm rot during the dormant summer months. Blue Pearl opens pale, silvery blue-lavender flowers with a bronzy-yellow base and a bright orange-yellow throat, the outer petals often showing a subtle bronze flush that gives the flower extra depth compared to solid-colored crocus cultivars. Blooming among the earliest crocus of the year, it works well massed in a rock garden, naturalized in a lawn, or tucked along a border edge where its small scale can be appreciated up close. Allow the grass-like foliage to die back naturally after flowering before mowing over naturalized plantings, and clumps will slowly multiply by cormlets to fill in over the years without needing regular division.

common_name: Jeanne d'Arc Crocus (Classic Large-Flowered Pure White Dutch Crocus)

planting.note: Plant corms in fall in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Jeanne d'Arc is a classic large-flowered Dutch crocus cultivar that naturalizes well in lawns and borders.

directions: Plant corms in fall in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Jeanne d'Arc naturalizes well in a lawn or border and multiplies steadily by cormlets over the years. Large, goblet-shaped, pure white flowers with faint violet feathering at the base and a bright orange-yellow throat open wide in full sun each early spring day, one of the longest-cultivated and most classic large-flowered Dutch crocus cultivars still widely grown today. Its clean white color makes it a versatile companion planted alongside purple or striped crocus cultivars for high-contrast spring drifts. Allow the grass-like foliage to die back naturally before mowing over a naturalized planting, and divide congested clumps during summer dormancy if flowering begins to decline after many years.

common_name: Flower Record Crocus (Classic Large-Flowered Purple Dutch Crocus)

planting.note: Plant corms in fall in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Flower Record is a classic large-flowered Dutch crocus cultivar prized for its rich, uniform purple color.

directions: Plant corms in fall in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Flower Record naturalizes well in a lawn or border and multiplies steadily by cormlets over the years. Large, goblet-shaped flowers open a rich, deep violet-purple with a subtle darker feathering at the base and a bright orange-yellow throat and stamens, a bold, saturated color that reads strongly even from a distance, making it one of the most widely planted large-flowered Dutch crocus cultivars for mass spring color. It opens wide in full sun each day and closes at night or in overcast weather to protect the pollen. Allow foliage to die back naturally before mowing over naturalized plantings, and divide congested clumps in summer dormancy if flowering begins to decline after many seasons.
